payload.rationale: I estimate a 10% chance of a qualifying delay past December 18, 2026. The supplied official-site evidence still advertises December 18 for North American theaters and IMAX, international release beginning December 16, and early-access screenings December 14–15. With approximately three months remaining, those specific advertised dates favor the release staying on schedule. The inference that this reflects substantial scheduling commitment is a judgment, not evidence that production or post-production is complete. The strongest reason my estimate could be too high is that the detailed rollout may reflect operational commitments that make a late postponement particularly unlikely. The strongest reason it could be too low is that an advertised date can remain unchanged despite undisclosed post-production problems or an impending studio scheduling decision. Earlier international or early-access screenings are supporting evidence of the planned rollout, not assumed substitutes for the contract-defined release threshold.
limitations: Only one official-site evidence record is supplied; there is no independent confirmation of production completion or release readiness.
No historical delay base rate or fitted probability model is available; the estimate is judgmental.
The full frozen contract rules are not supplied, leaving uncertainty about treatment of limited screenings, geography-specific changes, and announcements near the deadline.
An advertised schedule is not a guarantee against delay, and some site sections reportedly contain placeholder text.
